content: GPSM2, also known as LGN due to its 10 Leucine-Glycine-Asparagine (LGN) repeats, is a protein encoded by the GPSM2 gene in humans. Heterotrimeric G proteins are responsible for transducing extracellular signals, which are received by cell surface receptors, into coordinated intracellular responses. GPSM2 has been demonstrated to interact with nuclear mitotic apparatus protein 1 (NUMA1) and GNAI2 (G protein subunit alpha i2).
